title: Celsius to Fahrenheit
q: Convert the temperature in celsius to Fahrenheit (multiply by 9, divide by 5, add 32) and print the result.
ref:
fahrenheit = celsius * 9 / 5 + 32
print(fahrenheit)

ref:
total = 0
for n in numbers:
    total = total + n
print(total / len(numbers))

title: Keep only the odd ones
q: Build a new list that holds only the odd numbers, then print it.

title: Find the smallest
q: Find the smallest number in the list without using min(), then print it.

title: Running total
q: Build a list where each item is the sum of all numbers so far, then print it. For [1, 2, 3, 4] the idea is: 1, then 1+2, then 1+2+3, and so on.
ref:
running = []
total = 0
for n in numbers:
    total = total + n
    running.append(total)
print(running)

title: How many threes
q: Count how many times the number 3 appears in the list and print the count.

title: Print 1 to limit
q: Use range() to print every whole number from 1 up to and including limit, one per line.
ref:
for i in range(1, limit + 1):
    print(i)

title: Sum from 1 to n
q: Add up every whole number from 1 to n and print the total.
ref:
total = 0
for i in range(1, n + 1):
    total = total + i
print(total)

title: Factorial
q: Print the factorial of n (1 x 2 x 3 x ... x n).
ref:
result = 1
for i in range(1, n + 1):
    result = result * i
print(result)

title: Countdown
q: Use a while loop to print n, then n-1, and so on down to 1, one per line.

title: Halving
q: Count how many times n can be halved (whole-number division by 2) before it drops to 1 or less. Print the count.
ref:
count = 0
while n > 1:
    n = n // 2
    count = count + 1
print(count)

title: FizzBuzz
q: For every number from 1 to limit, print Fizz if it divides by 3, Buzz if it divides by 5, FizzBuzz if it divides by both, otherwise the number itself.

title: Fibonacci list
q: Build a list of the first count Fibonacci numbers (each one is the sum of the two before it, starting 0, 1) and print it.
ref:
fib = [0, 1]
while len(fib) < count:
    fib.append(fib[-1] + fib[-2])
print(fib)

title: Reverse a word

ref:
backwards = ""

title: Palindrome check
q: Print True if word reads the same forwards and backwards, otherwise False.
ref:
backwards = ""
for ch in word:
    backwards = ch + backwards
print(word == backwards)

title: Reverse a list
q: Build a new list with the items in reverse order and print it. Hint: range() can count backwards.
ref:
